model.rationale: Rick Crawford is an entrenched incumbent in an R+23 rural Arkansas district, outspending Terri Green by more than 80-to-1 in cash on hand, and prediction markets give him about a 98% win probability. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting any vulnerability, the fundamentals-based estimate of a Republican margin near 19 points stands.
model.watch: Only a dramatic national wave or an unforeseen scandal involving Crawford could narrow the margin, and even then a flip would require an unprecedented swing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arkansas's First District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+23. Rick Crawford, the Republican incumbent, is running for another term after securing his party's nomination. He enters the general election with a commanding financial advantage, having raised roughly $944,000 and holding more than $1 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Terri Green has raised about $65,000 and reported under $12,000 in cash. A Libertarian candidate, Steve Parsons, is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race, but prediction markets give Crawford roughly a 98 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's heavy Republican lean, Crawford's incumbency, and his overwhelming resource advantage makes a Democratic upset extremely unlikely. The realistic question is the size of Crawford's victory margin, not which party carries the seat.
